name: Fulvestrant
route_note: two 250 mg IM gluteal injections on days 1, 15 and 29, then monthly
owner: generic (many); Faslodex brand held by AstraZeneca

discovery.by: Alan Wakeling, Barry Bowler and colleagues, ICI
discovery.note: A steroidal 7α-alkylsulfinyl oestradiol analogue designed as a 'pure' anti-oestrogen without the partial agonism of tamoxifen.

tagline: Injectable pure anti-oestrogen that degrades the oestrogen receptor
summary: Fulvestrant is a steroidal oestrogen receptor antagonist that also triggers degradation of the receptor, without the partial agonist activity of tamoxifen. Given by monthly intramuscular injection, it is used in hormone-receptor-positive advanced breast cancer in postmenopausal women, alone or with CDK4/6, PI3K or AKT inhibitors.
mechanism: Fulvestrant binds the oestrogen receptor with high affinity; its long 7α side chain prevents receptor dimerisation and the conformational change needed for transcriptional activation.

The destabilised receptor is ubiquitinated and degraded by the proteasome, lowering ER levels in tumour cells. Because it has no agonist activity, it remains active after progression on tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors.
uses: HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer in postmenopausal women (first-line or after endocrine therapy)
In combination with palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib, alpelisib or capivasertib

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: ICI 182,780 identified as a pure anti-oestrogen.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved at 250 mg monthly for advanced breast cancer after anti-oestrogen therapy.

history.title: 500 mg dose
history.detail: CONFIRM trial leads to the higher 500 mg regimen with a loading dose.

history.title: FALCON
history.detail: Fulvestrant improves progression-free survival versus anastrozole in endocrine-naive advanced disease.

history.title: First-line approval
history.detail: FDA extends approval to endocrine-therapy-naive patients.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic fulvestrant becomes available in the US.

serious: bleeding or haematoma at injection site in patients with low platelets or on anticoagulants

facts: Its poor oral bioavailability spurred development of oral SERDs such as elacestrant.
